newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli unlinked bonds close higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli unlinked bonds close higher.

text.p: Israeli unlinked bonds and Makams closed higher on Sunday as investors predicted inflation would continue to decline in 1997, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.12 pct to 172.04
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.12 pct to 162.08
Volume was low at 144 million shekels with most activity concentrated in unlinked bonds.
"CPI-linked bonds closed mixed today with a negative bias as they came to a saturation point with yields falling to only 4.5 percent," said Ron Weisberg at IBI Investment House.
"Unlinked bonds continued to rise today on hopes for declining inflation. Bond prices reflect expectations for 1997 inflation of only nine percent," said a trader at Bank Discount.

"Yields on unlinked bonds fell sharply during the last month as investors predict that inflation will continue to decline and that the Bank of Israel will cut its key lending rate. With such low yields the unlinked bonds are becoming dangerous," Weisberg added.
"Demand for Makams (which are also unlinked) was very high today. During the last month yields fell from 15.5 percent to 14.3-14.6, which is very low," the Discount trader said.
Traders noted that dollar-linked bonds closed higher for the sixth consecutive day following the recent rise of the shekel against the U.S. currency.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
